name: Afrikaner nationalism
summary: Afrikaner nationalism holds the Afrikaners to be a distinct Calvinist, Afrikaans-speaking volk with a God-given land and task, entitled to govern itself. Its classic programme (Hertzog, the National Party, the FAK, Verwoerd) sought a republic free of the British crown, Afrikaans-medium Christian-national schooling and the separation of the races, later called apartheid or separate development. After 1994 the main strand shifted to self-determination and a volkstaat, treating apartheid as a failed model.
scope: The national question only: identity, territory, sovereignty, language, culture, religion in schooling, minorities and the means each strand accepts. Strands: the classic National Party/Hertzog/Verwoerd line, the Christian-national (Dutch Calvinist) education line, the post-1994 volkstaat line (Boshoff), and a white volksnationalist fringe (Vryburger, read for contrast only). The wider economic, welfare and foreign programmes of the National Party government and its apartheid laws are borrowing unless the nationalist texts state them as part of the national cause; positions only one strand states are null.

notes: Themes searched: national question, language, religion and schooling, race and minorities, republic and head of state, church-state, communism, immigration, economy, UN and Commonwealth. Economic, welfare, security, immigration and foreign policy positions are left null as the carrying government's programme (volkskapitalisme, Suppression of Communism, Commonwealth policy) or as Verwoerd alone. Racial segregation, franchise and trusteeship answers rest on the National Party programme of principles and Hertzog and Verwoerd; the post-1994 strand (Boshoff) calls the apartheid model a failure, so these are the doctrine at its peak, not today's. Blocked: Britannica pages (bot wall); the 1948 Beleid, Malan's and Hertzog's own speeches and the Broederbond constitution were not found as full text (Beleid known through Van Heyningen).
